name: jobs
description: Durable background jobs on SQLite: priorities, delays, unique keys, leases, retries with backoff, dead letters, workers and cron schedules

api.name: Cron
api.sig: pub type Cron = {source: Str, seconds: List[Int], minutes: List[Int], hours: List[Int], days: List[Int], months: List[Int], weekdays: List[Int], any_day: Bool, any_weekday: Bool, has_seconds: Bool} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A parsed cron expression. Each list holds the allowed values of one field in ascending order:
seconds 0-59 (only 0 for a 5-field expression), minutes 0-59, hours 0-23, days of the month
1-31, months 1-12 and days of the week 0-6 (0 is Sunday; 7 is read as 0). `any_day` and
`any_weekday` record whether those fields started with `*`, which decides how the two day fields
combine (see `cron_matches`).

api.name: parse_cron
api.sig: fn parse_cron(expr: Str) -> Res[Cron, Str]
api.doc:
Parses a cron expression: five fields (minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week), six
with a seconds field first, or a macro (`@yearly`, `@annually`, `@monthly`, `@weekly`, `@daily`,
`@midnight`, `@hourly`). Fields take `*`, numbers, `a-b` ranges, `/step` on any of them
(`*/15`, `1-30/5`, and `5/15` for `5-59/15`), comma lists, month names `JAN`-`DEC` and day names
`SUN`-`SAT` (any case); 0 and 7 are both Sunday. Errors name the field and the offending text.

api.name: cron_matches
api.sig: fn cron_matches(c: Cron, t: Time) -> Bool
api.doc:
Whether the instant `t` (to the second, in UTC) is a fire time of `c`. When both day fields are
restricted (neither starts with `*`), a day matches if either matches, as in Vixie cron:
`0 0 1 * MON` fires on the 1st and on every Monday. Otherwise both must match.

api.name: cron_matches_in
api.sig: fn cron_matches_in(c: Cron, z: Zone, t: Time) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `t` is a fire time of `c` on the wall clock of the zone `z`.

api.name: next_fire
api.sig: fn next_fire(c: Cron, t: Time) -> Opt[Time]
api.doc:
The first fire time of `c` strictly after `t`, in UTC, or none when there is none within nine
years (such as `0 0 30 2 *`).

api.name: prev_fire
api.sig: fn prev_fire(c: Cron, t: Time) -> Opt[Time]
api.doc: The last fire time of `c` at or before `t`, in UTC.

api.name: next_fires
api.sig: fn next_fires(c: Cron, t: Time, n: Int where _ >= 0) -> List[Time]
api.doc: The next `n` fire times of `c` after `t`, in UTC (fewer if the expression runs out).

api.name: next_fire_in
api.sig: fn next_fire_in(c: Cron, z: Zone, t: Time) -> Opt[Time]
api.doc:
The first fire time of `c` strictly after `t` on the wall clock of `z`, as an instant. Skipped
and repeated wall times follow the rules of daylight saving time described in the README.

api.name: prev_fire_in
api.sig: fn prev_fire_in(c: Cron, z: Zone, t: Time) -> Opt[Time]
api.doc: The last fire time of `c` at or before `t` on the wall clock of `z`, as an instant.

api.name: next_fires_in
api.sig: fn next_fires_in(c: Cron, z: Zone, t: Time, n: Int where _ >= 0) -> List[Time]
api.doc: The next `n` fire times of `c` after `t` on the wall clock of `z`.

api.name: State
api.sig: pub type State = Pending | Running | Completed | Dead | Cancelled derive Eq, Ord, Show
api.doc:
Where a job is in its life. `Pending` jobs wait for their `run_at` (a retry is a pending job
with attempts already made), `Running` jobs are leased to a worker, and the other three are
final: `Completed`, `Dead` (out of attempts or discarded: the dead letter set) and `Cancelled`.

api.name: NewJob
api.sig: pub type NewJob = {queue: Str where _.len > 0 and _.len <= 200, kind: Str where _.len > 0 and _.len <= 200, payload: Str, priority: Int where _ >= -1000 and _ <= 1000, run_at: Opt[Time], delay: Duration, max_attempts: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 1000, unique_key: Opt[Str], unique_for: Duration} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A job to enqueue. Build one with `job` and change fields with `with`. Smaller `priority` runs
first. `run_at` (when set) or `delay` (from the enqueue time) says when it becomes available.
With a `unique_key`, enqueueing again in the same queue while a job with that key is pending or
running, or within `unique_for` of the first one, returns the existing job instead.

api.name: AttemptError
api.sig: pub type AttemptError = {attempt: Int, at: Time, error: Str} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: One failed attempt, as recorded in `Job.errors`.

api.name: Job
api.sig: pub type Job = {id: Int, queue: Str, kind: Str, payload: Str, priority: Int, state: State, run_at: Time, attempts: Int, max_attempts: Int, unique_key: Opt[Str], last_error: Opt[Str], errors: List[AttemptError], created_at: Time, attempted_at: Opt[Time], finished_at: Opt[Time]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: A stored job.

api.name: Enqueued
api.sig: pub type Enqueued = Inserted{id: Int} | Duplicate{id: Int} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: The result of an enqueue: a new job, or the existing job with the same unique key.

api.name: Lease
api.sig: pub type Lease = {job: Job, token: Int, until: Time} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A claimed job. `token` identifies this claim: finishing calls with an older token (after the
lease expired and another worker claimed the job) change nothing and return false.

api.name: Outcome
api.sig: pub type Outcome = Done | Retry{error: Str} | RetryIn{error: Str, after: Duration} | Discard{error: Str} | Snooze{after: Duration} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
What a handler decided about a job. `Retry` waits by the worker's backoff and `RetryIn` by the
given time; both count the attempt, and a job out of attempts goes to `Dead`. `Discard` sends it
to `Dead` at once. `Snooze` runs it again later without counting the attempt.

api.name: Backoff
api.sig: pub type Backoff = Exponential{base: Duration, cap: Duration, jitter: F64} | Fixed{delay: Duration} | Linear{step: Duration, cap: Duration} | Steps{delays: List[Duration]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
How long to wait before the next attempt, by the number of attempts made (1 after the first).
`Exponential` doubles `base` up to `cap` and then takes off up to `jitter` (0 to 1) of it at
random but repeatably, seeded by the job id; `Linear` waits `step` times the attempt, up to `cap`;
`Steps` takes the list in order and repeats its last element.

api.name: Worker
api.sig: pub type Worker = {queue: Str where _.len > 0, lease: Duration, backoff: Backoff} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
What a worker needs: the queue it serves, how long a claim lasts before another worker may take
the job over, and the backoff for `Retry`.

api.name: Ran
api.sig: pub type Ran = Idle | Processed{job: Job, outcome: Outcome, recorded: Bool} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
What `work` did: nothing was available, or it ran a job, with whether the outcome was recorded
(false when the lease had been lost).

api.name: Filter
api.sig: pub type Filter = {queue: Opt[Str], state: Opt[State], kind: Opt[Str], after_id: Int, limit: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 1000} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
Filters for `list`: by queue, state and kind (none means any), job ids above `after_id` (for
keyset paging), at most `limit` jobs in id order.

api.name: QueueStats
api.sig: pub type QueueStats = {queue: Str, available: Int, scheduled: Int, running: Int, completed: Int, dead: Int, cancelled: Int, oldest_due: Opt[Time]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
Counts per queue. `available` are pending and due, `scheduled` pending and due later; `oldest_due`
is the earliest `run_at` of the available ones, a measure of how far behind the workers are.

api.name: migrate
api.sig: fn migrate(c: Db) -> Int ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc:
Creates or upgrades the tables this package uses (`jobs_jobs`, `jobs_schedules` and the version
table `jobs_schema`), each step in a transaction, and returns how many steps it applied. It is
separate from `db.migrate`, so an application's own migrations are not affected. Safe to call on
every start, from several processes.

api.name: job
api.sig: fn job(queue: Str where _.len > 0 and _.len <= 200, kind: Str where _.len > 0 and _.len <= 200, payload: Str) -> NewJob
api.doc:
A job for `queue` of kind `kind` with `payload` (usually JSON from `json.encode`): priority 0,
available at once, 20 attempts, not unique.

api.name: enqueue
api.sig: fn enqueue(c: Db, j: NewJob, now: Time) -> Enqueued ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: Adds a job at time `now`, or finds the pending, running or recent job with its unique key.

api.name: enqueue_all
api.sig: fn enqueue_all(c: Db, js: List[NewJob], now: Time) -> List[Enqueued] ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: Adds every job in one transaction: all of them or, if one fails, none. The results are in order.

api.name: enqueue_now
api.sig: fn enqueue_now(c: Db, j: NewJob) -> Enqueued ! db, fail[DbErr], time
api.doc: `enqueue` at the current time.

api.name: enqueued_id
api.sig: fn enqueued_id(e: Enqueued) -> Int
api.doc: The id of an enqueue result, new or existing.

api.name: get
api.sig: fn get(c: Db, id: Int) -> Opt[Job] ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: The job with id `id`.

api.name: filter
api.sig: fn filter() -> Filter
api.doc: Any queue, state and kind, from the start, 100 at a time.

api.name: list
api.sig: fn list(c: Db, f: Filter) -> List[Job] ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: Jobs that pass `f`, in id order. For the next page, set `after_id` to the last id returned.

api.name: stats
api.sig: fn stats(c: Db, now: Time) -> List[QueueStats] ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: Counts for every queue that has jobs, in queue order, at time `now`.

api.name: rescue
api.sig: fn rescue(c: Db, now: Time) -> Int ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc:
Returns jobs whose lease expired at `now` to their queues (or to dead when they were on their
last attempt) and gives how many. `claim` does this for its own queue, so call it only to see
crashed work sooner, for example from a periodic task.

api.name: claim_many
api.sig: fn claim_many(c: Db, queue: Str, n: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 1000, lease: Duration, now: Time) -> List[Lease] ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc:
Claims up to `n` available jobs of `queue` for `lease` from `now`, highest priority (smallest
number) first, then earliest `run_at`, then oldest. Each claim counts an attempt. The claim is one
`BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction, so concurrent workers in any number of threads or processes never
get the same job; expired leases of the queue are rescued first.

api.name: claim
api.sig: fn claim(c: Db, queue: Str, lease: Duration, now: Time) -> Opt[Lease] ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: Claims the next available job of `queue`, as `claim_many` with `n` = 1.

api.name: extend
api.sig: fn extend(c: Db, l: Lease, by: Duration, now: Time) -> Opt[Lease] ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: Extends a lease to `by` after `now` (a heartbeat for long jobs). None when the lease was lost.

api.name: complete
api.sig: fn complete(c: Db, l: Lease, now: Time) -> Bool ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc:
Marks a leased job completed. False when the lease was lost (the job was rescued and claimed
again, or cancelled).

api.name: fail_attempt
api.sig: fn fail_attempt(c: Db, l: Lease, error: Str, backoff: Backoff, now: Time) -> Bool ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc:
Records a failed attempt: the job runs again after `backoff`, or goes to dead when it has used
its attempts. False when the lease was lost.

api.name: retry_in
api.sig: fn retry_in(c: Db, l: Lease, error: Str, after: Duration, now: Time) -> Bool ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc:
Records a failed attempt that should run again after `after` (or go to dead when it has used its
attempts).

api.name: discard
api.sig: fn discard(c: Db, l: Lease, error: Str, now: Time) -> Bool ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: Sends a leased job to dead at once, whatever attempts it has left.

api.name: snooze
api.sig: fn snooze(c: Db, l: Lease, after: Duration, now: Time) -> Bool ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: Puts a leased job back to run after `after` without counting this attempt.

api.name: finish
api.sig: fn finish(c: Db, l: Lease, o: Outcome, backoff: Backoff, now: Time) -> Bool ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: Records a handler's outcome for a leased job, using `backoff` for `Retry`.

api.name: cancel
api.sig: fn cancel(c: Db, id: Int, now: Time) -> Bool ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: Cancels a pending or running job. A worker that still holds it can no longer record a result.

api.name: retry
api.sig: fn retry(c: Db, id: Int, now: Time) -> Bool ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: Makes a dead or cancelled job pending again, with its attempts reset and available at `now`.

api.name: retry_dead
api.sig: fn retry_dead(c: Db, queue: Str, now: Time) -> Int ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: `retry` for every dead job of `queue`; gives how many.

api.name: reschedule
api.sig: fn reschedule(c: Db, id: Int, at: Time) -> Bool ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: Moves a pending job to run at `at` (sooner or later). False for jobs in other states.

api.name: delete
api.sig: fn delete(c: Db, id: Int) -> Bool ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: Deletes a job in any state.

api.name: purge
api.sig: fn purge(c: Db, s: State, before: Time) -> Int ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc:
Deletes jobs in the final state `s` (`Completed`, `Dead` or `Cancelled`) that finished before
`before`, and gives how many. Pending and running jobs are never purged.

api.name: default_backoff
api.sig: fn default_backoff() -> Backoff
api.doc: Exponential backoff from 1 second up to 1 hour, with a quarter of jitter.

api.name: backoff_delay
api.sig: fn backoff_delay(b: Backoff, attempt: Int where _ >= 0, seed: Int) -> Duration
api.doc:
The wait before the attempt after `attempt` attempts, for a job seeded by `seed` (its id): the
same inputs always give the same wait, so retries are spread out but repeatable in tests.

api.name: worker
api.sig: fn worker(queue: Str where _.len > 0) -> Worker
api.doc: A worker for `queue` with a 5 minute lease and the default backoff.

api.name: work_at
api.sig: fn work_at[e](c: Db, w: Worker, handler: Job -> Outcome ! e, now: Time) -> Ran ! db, fail[DbErr], e
api.doc:
Claims one job of the worker's queue at `now`, runs `handler` on it and records the outcome at
`now`. Handlers report failure through their `Outcome`; a handler that traps or never returns
leaves the job leased, and it is retried when the lease expires.

api.name: work
api.sig: fn work[e](c: Db, w: Worker, handler: Job -> Outcome ! e) -> Ran ! db, fail[DbErr], time, e
api.doc: `work_at` with the clock: claims now and records the outcome when the handler returns.

api.name: drain
api.sig: fn drain[e](c: Db, w: Worker, handler: Job -> Outcome ! e, max: Int where _ >= 0) -> Int ! db, fail[DbErr], time, e
api.doc:
Runs `work` until the queue has nothing available or `max` jobs ran, and gives how many ran.
For concurrency, start several in `par` and pass a top-level function (or a lambda written
inside the task), since tasks can't share function values:
`for i in par(0..4)` then `jobs.drain(c, w, send_email, 1000)`.

api.name: run_worker
api.sig: fn run_worker[e](c: Db, w: Worker, handler: Job -> Outcome ! e, stop: Atomic[Int], idle_ms: Int where _ >= 1) -> Int ! db, fail[DbErr], time, conc, div, e
api.doc:
Serves the worker's queue until `stop` holds a non-zero value: runs jobs while there are any and
sleeps `idle_ms` when there are none. Gives how many jobs ran. Set `stop` from another task, or
from a signal-handling path of the program, to finish after the current job.

api.name: Missed
api.sig: pub type Missed = CatchUp{limit: Int} | Latest | Skip{grace: Duration} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
What `tick` does about fire times that passed while nothing ticked (the process was down):
`CatchUp` enqueues each of them, at most the `limit` most recent; `Latest` enqueues only the most
recent; `Skip` enqueues the most recent only if it is at most `grace` old, and drops the rest.

api.name: Schedule
api.sig: pub type Schedule = {name: Str where _.len > 0 and _.len <= 200, cron: Str, zone: Str, queue: Str where _.len > 0 and _.len <= 200, kind: Str where _.len > 0 and _.len <= 200, payload: Str, priority: Int where _ >= -1000 and _ <= 1000, max_attempts: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 1000, missed: Missed, enabled: Bool} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A recurring job: `cron` (see `parse_cron`) on the wall clock of the IANA zone `zone` (`"UTC"`,
`"Europe/Berlin"`, or a fixed offset such as `"+05:30"`), enqueueing `kind` with `payload` into
`queue`. `name` identifies it.

api.name: Fired
api.sig: pub type Fired = {schedule: Str, at: Time, result: Enqueued} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: One run that `tick` enqueued: the schedule, its fire time and the enqueue result.

api.name: schedule
api.sig: fn schedule(name: Str where _.len > 0 and _.len <= 200, cron: Str, queue: Str where _.len > 0 and _.len <= 200, kind: Str where _.len > 0 and _.len <= 200, payload: Str) -> Schedule
api.doc:
A schedule named `name` in UTC, enabled, with priority 0, 20 attempts and `Latest` for missed
runs.

api.name: put_schedule
api.sig: fn put_schedule(c: Db, s: Schedule, now: Time) -> Res[Unit, Str] ! db, fail[DbErr], time
api.doc:
Adds or replaces the schedule `s.name`, checking its cron expression and zone. Its first run is
the first fire time after `now`; replacing a schedule with the same expression and zone keeps
its progress, so nothing fires twice. An error names what is wrong.

api.name: remove_schedule
api.sig: fn remove_schedule(c: Db, name: Str) -> Bool ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: Removes a schedule. Jobs it already enqueued stay.

api.name: set_enabled
api.sig: fn set_enabled(c: Db, name: Str, enabled: Bool, now: Time) -> Bool ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc:
Turns a schedule on or off. Turning one on counts from `now`, so the time it was off is not
caught up.

api.name: schedules
api.sig: fn schedules(c: Db) -> List[Schedule] ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: Every schedule, by name.

api.name: due_fires
api.sig: fn due_fires(c: Cron, z: Zone, last: Time, now: Time, missed: Missed) -> List[Time]
api.doc:
The fire times of `c` in `z` after `last` and at or before `now` that `missed` lets through,
oldest first. `tick` enqueues these.

api.name: tick
api.sig: fn tick(c: Db, now: Time) -> List[Fired] ! db, fail[DbErr], time
api.doc:
Enqueues every run of every enabled schedule that is due at `now`, once: each run gets the unique
key `schedule:NAME:MILLIS` and the schedule's progress moves to `now` in the same transaction, so
ticking from several processes, or twice, enqueues nothing twice. Call it every few seconds or
every minute; missed runs follow each schedule's `missed`.
